messages.m0089: A few things you might be wondering.
messages.m0090: Can I upload a report today?
messages.m0091: Yes, in the local application. Sign in, upload a PDF or image and confirm the extracted values. If extraction is unavailable, use manual entry or import the fictional three-year sample. In-app follow-ups and PDF export work; email reminders are not connected.
messages.m0092: Can it tell me whether I have a condition?
messages.m0093: No. HealthMatch AI is a health information and self-management tool, not a diagnostic service. A clinician must interpret results in the context of your health.
messages.m0094: What if I only have one report?
messages.m0095: The planned first-report reading helps explain individual results. Comparable results from two or more dates will unlock longitudinal trends.
messages.m0096: Who decides the severity and follow-up timing?
messages.m0097: Auditable, versioned rules will determine severity, red flags, and follow-up intervals. AI will extract results and explain those decisions; it will not make clinical judgments. You will confirm the extracted values first.
messages.m0099: The local pilot covers HbA1c, glucose, potassium, ALT and hemoglobin. Other markers retain their original values and remain unclassified. A broader library of roughly 120 markers requires clinical review before release.
messages.m0101: The public sample is fictional. The local app stores encrypted report data and provides export and workspace deletion. Files sent for extraction go to the configured Gemini endpoint with your consent. See Privacy for local HTTP, retention and deletion limits; this is not a production health-data service.

messages.m0236: Do not wait for an app in an emergency.
messages.m0237: If a laboratory or clinician tells you a result is critical, seek urgent medical attention and follow their instructions. If you believe you are having a medical emergency, contact local emergency services. This app is not continuously monitored.
messages.m0239: HealthMatch AI is designed to help you understand reports and manage follow-ups. It will not provide diagnostic conclusions, prescriptions, medication advice, symptom triage, or access to a doctor marketplace. It cannot guarantee early detection or rule out illness.
messages.m0241: The local application uses versioned, auditable rules for four severity levels: normal, mild deviation, significant abnormality, and critical. Separate red-flag rules show critical-value warnings at the top of the first screen, immediately and without a paywall.
messages.m0242: AI extracts report information or selects relevant evidence and a question topic. Answers use validated, report-specific templates. You must confirm extracted values before they enter your health record. Generated explanations must pass checks against the rule outputs before display; a safe template will replace an explanation that fails validation.
messages.m0244: Readings will use the report’s own reference intervals and applicable thresholds from public guidelines. Each rule must include a source, version, population, unit, and review record. Reference intervals vary by laboratory and context; incomplete or incompatible results must not be labeled normal by default.
messages.m0245: Uncovered markers will show the original report value and “interpretation not yet covered.” A normal result or no alert is not an assurance of health. Five markers currently have local pilot rules: HbA1c, glucose, potassium, ALT and hemoglobin. Clinical sign-off is pending. Follow-up intervals are clinician-review targets, not universal repeat-test instructions.
messages.m0247: The local app encrypts saved health payloads and separates fictional samples from personal reports. Upload extraction sends files to the configured Gemini endpoint with consent; manual entry and sample import need no model access.
messages.m0248: Local connections use loopback HTTP. Active workspace data can be exported or deleted, but device backups, SQLite journals and provider-retained copies are outside this control. Production privacy and deletion requirements are not complete.
messages.m0249: Read actual local privacy controls and limits →
messages.m0252: This notice describes the local phase 2 application. It has not been deployed as a production health-data service. Use fictional data for local evaluation.
messages.m0261: Accounts and sessions use the existing D1 data layer, running locally through Cloudflare’s emulator. Report values, source text, drafts, self-reported profiles and task state are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being stored in the local database. Account email and technical record identifiers are not encrypted by the application. The encryption key is kept in an ignored local environment file.
messages.m0262: The browser and API run on this computer over loopback HTTP; this is not encrypted transport. External model requests use HTTPS. Production TLS, key management and hosting locations have not been established.
messages.m0264: With your permission, uploaded PDF/image bytes are sent to the configured Gemini API endpoint for extraction. With report Q&A enabled, your question and confirmed marker values are sent to select relevant evidence and an answer topic. By default personal-workspace Q&A uses templates until you opt in. Sample data is fictional and kept separate.
messages.m0265: The current default endpoint is Google’s Gemini API at generativelanguage.googleapis.com. An operator may configure a different endpoint. Processing locations, provider retention and contractual safeguards are not verified for production use. Model access is optional: Sample import, manual entry, rules and template answers work without it.
messages.m0267: Original uploads are processed transiently and are not stored by this app. A browser preview may remain until the page closes. Saved values, source text and pending drafts remain until you delete the selected workspace. In Health profile, export all workspace data as JSON or delete its profile, reports, drafts and reminder records. Personal and Sample workspaces are deleted separately.
messages.m0268: Deletion removes active records; it does not erase downloaded files, device backups, SQLite journals/free pages or copies retained by an external model provider. No remote-provider deletion API or backup expiry process is implemented. These limits must be resolved before a production launch claiming complete erasure. Account/session records are managed separately by the existing login service.
messages.m0270: The new application does not sell health data or use it for advertising. No analytics scripts are loaded by these pages. In-app reminders are available; reminder email is not connected and sends nothing. Local development login links do not send email or verify email ownership.
messages.m0272: Clinical rule approval, processor contracts, processing countries, GDPR legal basis and user-rights handling, retention schedules, encrypted transport, operational security and verified complete-deletion procedures remain release requirements. This pilot makes no production compliance claim.
